observations: Torah #96 is a short practical teaching — a direct personal exhortation to practice hitbodedut — and does not contain the structural bechina framework required to form concept packages. A new package requires 3 or more concepts connected by explicit bechina language in the source text, forming an independent thematic domain. This teaching contains no explicit bechina declarations. The key concepts present — הִתְבּוֹדְדוּת (hitbodedut/personal prayer), דִּבּוּר (speech), and implicitly תְּפִלָּה (prayer, via the Talmudic citation) — are used in descriptive and practical roles rather than as declared bechina equivalences of each other. The Rebbe does not say 'hitbodedut is a bechina of prayer' or 'speech is a bechina of hitbodedut'; he says practice hitbodedut, even one word has power, and would that a person prays all day. The only structurally suggestive element is the implicit identification of hitbodedut with tefillah (the Talmud quote seamlessly equates them as the same practice), but even this is not framed as a bechina declaration — it is an illustrative citation, not a conceptual equation. The power-of-speech aside (the gun-whisper illustration) is a supporting argument for persistence, not a bechina cluster. Therefore no new packages are proposed for this Torah.
